headline: Sequencing analysis tools are being tuned for speed, memory behavior, and accuracy
label: Scalable Sequencing Data Computation
summary: Recent preprints and a publication report large speedups and systems-level profiling for sequencing analysis, alongside accuracy benchmarks.
synthesis: The common thread is computation applied close to primary sequencing data, where accuracy and efficiency are evaluated together. ScanFold3 reports 38-129x gains over ScanFold2 for RNA secondary structure scanning, using greedy approximate matching and C++ optimization. brisc runs a multithreaded CPU workflow on 10M single cells in 3 minutes and is reproducible across thread counts. Cycle-Extractor reconstructs ecDNA cycles from short- or long-read breakpoint graphs as a MILP and is reported to outperform AmpliconArchitect and Decoil. The arXiv characterization of WGA, long-read, and short-read mappers using VTune and DAMOV-SIM identifies memory-bound functions and cache behavior. What is new here is pairing algorithmic or read-level inputs with explicit systems-level measurement. The items address distinct biological problems, so the shared element is methodological rather than biological.
